source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: During colostomy irrigation, the bag is hung:
questions.rationale: Hang the bag at shoulder level or 12–18 inches above the stoma, using 500–1,000 mL of warm solution.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 7 Colostomy irrigation (PDF p. 194)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Cramping occurs during colostomy irrigation. The nurse should:
options: Clamp the tubing until it passes
questions.rationale: Clamp the tubing and resume when cramping subsides.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 7 Colostomy irrigation (PDF p. 194)
questions.quote: If cramping occurs during irrigation, clamp tubing; release tubing as cramping subsides.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which type of colostomy is usually irrigated to regulate bowel movements?
questions.rationale: Sigmoid colostomies pass formed stool and can be regulated by irrigation; ileostomies are never irrigated.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 7 Colostomy irrigation (PDF p. 194)
questions.quote: This is recommended with sigmoid colostomy because the fecal waste is hard.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which food can help reduce ostomy odor?
questions.rationale: Yogurt, buttermilk and parsley reduce odor; cabbage, eggs, fish and onions increase it.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 7 Managing odor (PDF p. 194)
questions.quote: Include foods that reduce odor, e.g., yogurt, parsley, buttermilk

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with a new colostomy refuses to look at the stoma. The nurse should first:
questions.rationale: Encourage verbalization of fears and concerns; readiness to learn shows when he starts asking about care.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 7 Teaching for self-care (PDF p. 195)
questions.quote: Ifthe client refuses to look at the stoma, encourage him to verbalize his feelings, fears and concerns about the stoma.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client asks if touching his stoma will hurt. The nurse explains that the stoma:
questions.rationale: The stoma has no touch or pain sensation, so it must be protected from unnoticed trauma.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 7 Stoma care (PDF p. 195)
questions.quote: Inform client that the stoma has no touch or pain sensation.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: After hemorrhoidectomy, warm sitz baths are best done:
questions.rationale: Ice for the first 12 hours, then sitz baths, ideally after defecation, to relieve pain and clean the area.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 7 Hemorrhoidectomy (PDF p. 196)
questions.quote: The best time to do the procedure is after bowel movement.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: After hemorrhoidectomy, the nurse monitors closely for:
questions.rationale: Pain and spasm near the anus often cause urinary retention after anorectal surgery.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 7 Hemorrhoidectomy (PDF p. 196)
questions.quote: Monitor the client for urinary retention.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: An infant has colicky pain, draws up the knees and passes 'currant jelly' stools. The nurse suspects:
questions.rationale: Intussusception: colicky pain, currant jelly stools (blood and mucus), sausage-shaped mass.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 7 Intussusception (PDF p. 196)
questions.quote: Currant jelly stools (stools containing blood and mucus).

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: After hydrostatic reduction for intussusception, which sign shows success?
questions.rationale: Passing normal brown stool indicates the intussusception has resolved; notify the physician.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 7 Intussusception (PDF p. 197)
questions.quote: Monitor for the passage of normal, brown stool. This indicates resolution of intussusception.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client's abdominal incision opens and bowel loops protrude. The nurse's first action is to:
questions.rationale: Evisceration: cover with sterile saline-soaked dressing, position with knees flexed, never replace organs, call the surgeon.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 7 Evisceration (PDF p. 198)
questions.quote: Cover the wound with sterile dressings moistened with normal saline.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: For a client with evisceration, which position is best?
questions.rationale: Supine or semi-Fowler's with knees flexed relaxes abdominal muscles and prevents further protrusion.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 7 Evisceration (PDF p. 198)
questions.quote: Place in supine or semi — Fowler's position with knees flexed.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client on long-term antibiotics develops frequent watery diarrhea. Which isolation is needed if C. difficile is confirmed?
questions.rationale: C. difficile spreads fecal-orally; use contact precautions and soap-and-water handwashing.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 7 Clostridium difficile (PDF p. 198)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Why are opioid antidiarrheals avoided when diarrhea is caused by bacterial toxins?
questions.rationale: Slowing the bowel keeps toxins and organisms in longer, worsening the condition.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 7 Antidiarrheals (PDF p. 199)
questions.quote: They may worsen the condition by delaying the elimination of toxins.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Dermatitis, diarrhea and dementia point to deficiency of:
questions.rationale: Pellagra (niacin deficiency) causes dermatitis, diarrhea, dementia and, if untreated, death.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 7 Pellagra (PDF p. 199)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A BMI of 27 is classified as:
questions.rationale: BMI 18.5–24.9 normal, 25–29.9 overweight, 30 and above obese (standard WHO cutoffs).
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 7 Body mass index (PDF p. 200)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with a bleeding duodenal ulcer suddenly has severe epigastric pain and a rigid, board-like abdomen. This suggests:
questions.rationale: Sudden sharp pain with board-like rigidity indicates perforation and peritonitis, an emergency.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 7 Answers and rationales (PDF p. 204)
questions.quote: Perforated ulcer causes peritonitis as manifested by sudden sharp pain, with rigid, boardlike abdomen.
